title: Length-eight F4 higher OM residual extension
objective: Certify the generic bounded v429 p=2 F4 higher-residual effective-length-8 OM extension with exact finite-field residual, mixed-radix quotient, closure, index, corruption, PARI-local HNF, and benchmark evidence while keeping automatic selection disabled

oracles: Sage/PARI exact local index and frozen maximal-order lattice

handoff.summary: Certifies the v429 p=2 F4 effective-length-eight boundary through a generic bounded recursive residual operator and exact finite-field mixed-radix lifts. The tree has two degree-32 terminal branches and local index 332; its independently multiplication-closed quotient HNF is byte-for-byte equal to the localization of the frozen PARI maximal-order lattice. CPython and Sage.js focused witnesses pass, a corrupted basis is rejected, and the benchmark records 1.84s versus 48.74s while keeping automatic selection disabled.
risks: The proved recursive domain is bounded to active depth four, effective residual length eight, linear residual towers after the first extension, and sixteen representative refinements per level; every exceeded bound fails closed.

The broad pnpm test:native run was intentionally interrupted with exit 130 at the coordinator's request after cache restoration and the compiler/build stages, to release resources for final degree-90 corpus verification. No native failure had appeared, but no passing receipt was recorded.
The inherited length-four test still asserts that this p=2 case is incomplete and must be updated by the integration lane alongside registration of the new focused test.
Only linux-x64 was exercised in this lane; integration CI retains responsibility for the other declared first-class platforms.
next_steps: Update the inherited p=2 incomplete assertions and register test/number-field-om-length8.cjs from the integration lane.
Rerun the broad native and platform matrix when it no longer contends with corpus certification.
Keep public automatic OM selection disabled until the measured 48.74s Sage.js certificate establishes a favorable end-to-end crossover.
